research.proposedTitle: Beaver Lake permit withdrawals leave public commitments in question
research.proposedSummary: LDEQ records list June 2026 permit application withdrawals for Beaver Lake in Rapides Parish. Earlier official records document proposed state incentives, tax exemption decisions and port infrastructure authorizations. A replacement tenant, land option terms and the current disposition of public commitments are not established by the retained official evidence. The port's September 30, 2026 minutes record its executive director's comment that SunGas concluded its engagement with the port and paid the port's expenditures in full; attribute that statement and do not turn it into a payment amount or a statement about other public commitments.

claims.text: In July 2023, Louisiana Economic Development announced that SunGas was considering a roughly $1.8 billion methanol facility in Rapides Parish.

supports.excerpt: PINEVILLE, La. – SunGas Renewables, an independent division of GTI Energy, announced it is considering an investment of approximately $1.8 billion to establish a renewable low-carbon methanol production facility in Rapides Parish. The company projects its Pineville facility, Beaver Lake Renewable Energy (BLRE), would manufacture nearly 400,000 metric tons of green methanol per year for SunGas customers worldwide.
supports.section: Opening description of the proposed Beaver Lake facility

claims.text: The July 2023 announcement projected 109 direct jobs and about 1,150 jobs at peak construction if the project proceeded.

supports.excerpt: If the project moves forward as outlined, the company expects to create 109 new direct jobs with an average annual salary of more than $78,000. SunGas also anticipates the creation of about 1,150 construction jobs at peak construction. Louisiana Economic Development estimates the project would result in an additional 390 new indirect jobs, for a total of 499 new jobs in central Louisiana.
supports.section: Conditional employment projections

claims.text: The 2023 proposal placed Beaver Lake at the former International Paper facility in Rapides Parish.

supports.excerpt: BLRE would be built at the site of the former International Paper facility in Rapides Parish, which has been vacant since 2009. A front-end engineering and design (FEED) study on the site is planned in October. The company expects to make a final investment decision in August 2024, and to begin construction beginning by the end of that year. It anticipates commercial operations to commence in 2027.
supports.section: Proposed location and original schedule

claims.text: The state prepared a $6 million infrastructure grant conditioned on investment and employment targets, according to the July 2023 announcement.

supports.excerpt: To support the project in Pineville, the state of Louisiana has prepared a competitive incentives package that includes the comprehensive workforce development solutions of LED FastStart and a $6 million performance-based grant for infrastructure improvements upon meeting investment and employment targets. If the project moves forward, the company is expected to participate in the state’s Quality Jobs and Industrial Tax Exemption programs.
supports.section: Proposed state incentives and performance conditions

knownUnknowns: The retained official sources do not identify a replacement tenant or establish the terms of the reported 2026 land option.

The retained records authorize or propose public support. Apart from the port executive director's September 30, 2026 comment that SunGas paid the port's expenditures in full, they do not establish how much has been disbursed or whether commitments have been cancelled or reassigned.
The March 2026 FastSites announcement does not give a funding amount for Beaver Lake.
The current status of Beaver Lake's industrial tax exemption after the 2026 permit withdrawals is not established by these records.
The saved LDEQ records identify permit withdrawal documents. Full letters and the underlying permit files are not included in the retained evidence.
These sources do not establish a current public hearing, open comment period or confirmed replacement project.
The September 30, 2026 port minutes do not give the amount SunGas paid, do not name Beaver Lake or Beaver Lake Renewable Energy, and do not address the Red River Waterway Commission funds.
research.reviewResponsibility: Owner review of named official sources, including Red River Waterway Commission and Central Louisiana Regional Port minutes, by January 15, 2027. Source checks are manual.
